newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cost-cutting plan to cut '97 oper deficit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cost-cutting plan to cut '97 oper deficit.

text.p: A package of cost-cutting measures announced by the Brazilian government Friday may cut the operational deficit to below 2.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997, the government said in a statement.

"Once adopted, these measures...allow us to forecast a consolidated operational deficit of less than 2.5 percent of GDP in 1997," said the statement, signed by the finance, planning, social security and adminstration ministers.
The document outlined measures to cut federal costs and increase revenue.

Among the measures are the hiring of 2,000 new tax officials, simplification of the tax system, measures to contain spending by state firms on administration costs and staff benefits and to trim a range of civil servants' perks.

The public sector operational deficit in the first seven months of 1996 reached 3.72 percent of GDP, compared with an original government target of halving last year's 5.0 percent of GDP operational deficit.
The cost-cutting package is intended to show the government can tackle the deficit without solely relying on the passage of fiscal reforms through Congress, officials say.
But the ministers noted in their statement, "It's worth bearing in mind that these initiatives do not eliminate the need and the urgency for approval of constitutional changes underway in Congress."
